subject: Request: subprocessor dataflow certification required for onboarding
messages:
From: Sarah Duncan <sarah.duncan@aurorapay.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: compliance@aurorapay.com
Date: 2027-11-03T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Request: subprocessor roster & dataflow certification for onboarding

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the quick responses on contract timing last week. As part of AuroraPay's procurement checklist we need a current subprocessor roster and a short certification that describes how Redwood routes or prevents Aurora customer data from transiting third countries where we have residency constraints. Our legal team flags two specific asks: 

- A spreadsheet listing all subprocessors (name, primary function, country of processing, whether encryption at rest is applied, and whether they receive plaintext content).
- A one-paragraph statement from Redwood describing what controls prevent cross-border routing for EU-resident data and whether temporary fallback processors are used in a failover scenario.

We'd like these by EOD Friday (2027-11-05) to keep the onboarding slot. I've attached a template for the roster to speed this up.

Attachments: aurorapay_subprocessors_20271103.xlsx (template)

Happy to hop on a call if helpful.

Best,
Sarah Duncan
Head of Procurement, AuroraPay

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Duncan <sarah.duncan@aurorapay.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-03T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor roster & dataflow certification for onboarding

Hi Sarah — thanks, and hi team.

Vanessa here — looping in Kimberly (privacy & vendor clearance) and Marcus (solutions/sales ops) so we can get you a complete pack. Quick clarifying points before we populate the template: 

1) There is one component that sometimes causes confusion: our telemetry aggregator (EdgeBridge) is contracted as an "observability agent" and performs ephemeral buffering in the US and EU regions. For EU-resident workload we have configuration flags to prevent cross-border buffering, but those flags are per-customer and depend on routing policy. Can you confirm whether Aurora requires a technical attestation that EdgeBridge will never buffer EU-origin traffic outside EU under any failure mode, or whether an operational fallback (onshore standby) is acceptable?

2) Do you need the DPA clause references (section numbers) alongside each subprocessor entry, or is the roster + short statement sufficient for procurement? We can also share the DPA addendum we've prepared for Aurora (attached) to speed legal review.

We'll aim to return the filled roster and the one-paragraph routing statement by your deadline, but if the attestation you require is stricter than our standard onshore-fallback approach we may need a short procurement pause while we run the legal ask through our infra team.

Proposed next step: short 30-minute sync tomorrow afternoon (Vanessa / Kimberly / Marcus / Sarah) to confirm the level of attestation and the list scoping. Available windows: 11/04 2:00–3:30pm PT or 11/04 4:00–5:00pm PT.

Thanks — Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai

From: Sarah Duncan <sarah.duncan@aurorapay.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: compliance@aurorapay.com
Date: 2027-11-03T20:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor roster & dataflow certification for onboarding

Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the detail. Short answers below: 

- Procurement would prefer a technical attestation that EdgeBridge (or any named observability vendor) will not persist or buffer EU-resident personal data outside EU in any normal or degraded mode. If there is a documented operational onshore fallback, that is acceptable only if you also provide frequent test evidence of failover and a contractual clause that commits to onshore-only buffering for Aurora EU data.
- For now the roster + short statement is the priority; legal will ask for DPA clause references later.

I've attached our filled template with current expectations to help illustrate what we need — note the column on "required attestation: yes/no".

Attachments: aurorapay_subprocessors_20271103.xlsx

If you can do the 2:00–3:30pm PT slot tomorrow that works. We can treat the call as operational + legal alignment.

Best,
Sarah

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Cc: Sarah Duncan <sarah.duncan@aurorapay.com>
Date: 2027-11-04T09:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor roster & dataflow certification for onboarding

Kimberly, Marcus — copying the ask and Aurora's preference. TL;DR: procurement wants explicit onshore-only buffering guarantee for EU-origin Aurora traffic or contract clause + regular failover test evidence.

Action items I propose before the sync at 2:00pm PT: 

- Kimberly: can you prepare a one-paragraph routing certification (company letterhead) that describes our standard routing controls and the conditions under which EdgeBridge would buffer outside-region? If we cannot provide a full technology-level attestation, include proposed contract language that commits to onshore-only buffering for Aurora EU data and indicates the cadence of failover tests (e.g., quarterly).
- Marcus: please confirm whether we need to hold onboarding until the attestation/contract language is signed, or whether we can proceed with a conditional onboarding (limited traffic profile) while contract is in flight. Put the commercial suggestion in the call so we have a clear customer-facing position.

Also attaching the DPA addendum draft we drafted for Aurora to show the clause placement. If legal wants edits, Kimberly I can get your markups before sending.

Attachments: rwi_dpa_addendum_draft_v1.pdf

Onward — Vanessa
